content.title: How The 'First Sale Rule' Is Helping Many Businesses Work Around Tariff Costs
content.summary: U.S. companies are using a 1988 customs law called the "first sale rule" to get around new tariffs The law allows importers to use the price of the first sale in a series of transactions rather than its import price to calculate potential levies Mocler and Traeger are among the companies that have openly discussed implementing the law to lower tariff impacts A decades-old piece of legislation is helping many businesses mitigate the worst effects of the tariffs, CNBC reports.
